synthNotes: Treat every At Sea Journal row as ONE author, Erik Germani (the site index confirms the byline; the JSON splits it three ways). State the aggregate concentration: Books and Boots, At Sea Journal and Wikipedia together are about a third of kept rows. Mark where a rule CORRECTS Martin rather than follows him (the previous section did so silently at features 16, 21 and 25). Reconcile these self-contradictions the previous critic found, and say how: - **What counts as an old word.** Feature 1 makes reeve, tithe, hide, ward the archivist's everyday stock; feature 5 lists reeve, tithe, wergild, glebe, assart as "archaisms with real dates"; feature 6 rations "one old word in a paragraph; three is a costume". The same word is both base lexicon and rationed salt. The section never draws the line between native-root modern words (unrestricted) and dated archaisms (rationed). - **Mayhaps.** Feature 5 allows the older form in an elder's or a charter's mouth (Aemon's mayhaps); feature 7 bars mayhaps and must needs flat. Feature 7 needs "in the archivist's own voice". - **Four rules for the first sentence.** Feature 28: a shot, where the light falls. Feature 31: the season, by one sense, once. Feature 33: the concrete thing, never a summary. Feature 35: the one strange fact about the settlement. Not reconciled, and 31 rests on #124, which the verifier says not to cite for it. - **Distance.** Feature 21 fixes the archivist at "a fixed middle distance" that "does not move"; feature 28 makes the first sentence a director's shot; feature 15 walks the reader through the town in one sentence. Either the archivist moves or the shot is barred. - **Feature 25 corrects Martin without saying so.** Its rule bars any saying "borrowed from the reader's world"; its evidence [50] is that Martin mixes real proverbs with adapted and invented ones. Same unflagged correction at feature 21 (one name form; Germani's point is that Martin cycles four) and feature 16 (semicolon banned; Germani says Martin mastered it). Section K of v1 admitted taking the critics' side on tics; this section has no such admission. - **Feature 39 halves its source.** "A few score" against 154 with SD 47; the spread is dropped, the halving is unexplained. - **Voice counts.** Feature 31 says three voices and lists four (LitCharts, The Fantasy Review, Germani, Auerbach). Feature 33 says five and lists six (Germani, Hughes, Auerbach, Turner, Weed, Martin). Feature 20 counts "Richards via Wikipedia" as a sixth voice on the same Wikipedia page as [29]. Feature 26 says six and names five.
